sections.h2: Where do I search Escambia County property records?
sections.html:
Deeds and other recorded land documents are searched on the Clerk's Landmark Web official records site, and tax and value data are on the Property Appraiser and Tax Collector sites. The Clerk of the Circuit Court and Comptroller keeps the official records, and its Landmark Web page offers searches by name, document, case number, book and page, consideration, record date, clerk file number and legal description.

The Property Appraiser's site at escpa.org covers parcels in Escambia County, the City of Pensacola and the Town of Century, with values reflecting the 2026 certified roll. The Tax Collector's site lets you search a tax account by name, address or account number. Parcel data on the appraiser's site is not survey quality, so use a surveyor for boundaries.

sections.h2: What older records does the Escambia County Clerk hold?
sections.html:
The Clerk's Public Records Center keeps court, board and marriage records, plus a set of historical files that can only be viewed in person. Those historical items matter for old titles and family property.

  • Circuit civil files from 1820 to 1985
  • The Government Survey of 1827
  • Marriage books from 1822 to 1999
  • Old wills and will books from the 1800s
  • Probate cases from 1883 to 1997
  • The Spanish Census of Pensacola, 1820

Online court records require registration, and the Clerk's page links to a registration agreement form and a guide to searching. The Clerk also lists Escambia County mortgage foreclosure sales on its Online Public Records page.

sections.h2: What are the clerk's charges for putting a deed on the Escambia record?
sections.html:
The charges come from a statewide schedule, so the clerk in Pensacola charges what clerks elsewhere do. The statute prints $5.00 on page one, $4.00 on each page after, and a $1.00 add-on for names beyond the fourth.

Clerk recording charges in Florida Statutes s. 28.24(13)
ChargeAmount printed in the statute
First page$5.00
Each added page$4.00
Each name beyond four$1.00
Records modernization fund, first page$1.00
Records modernization fund, each added page$0.50
Added technology charge$4 per page

Ask the Clerk for the current total on your document, because page size and name count change the bill. The Clerk collects deed stamp tax at the same counter.

sections.h2: What documentary stamp tax applies to an Escambia County deed?
sections.html:
Escambia County uses the standard Florida rate of 70 cents per $100 of consideration. Florida DOR reserves the lower Miami-Dade rate for that county alone.

Consideration includes cash, a discharged obligation and any mortgage on the property, whether or not the buyer assumes it. Every party to the deed is liable for the tax no matter who agrees to pay, and the clerk collects it at recording. Mortgages and notes carry 35 cents per $100 secured, with a cap of $2,450 on a note and no cap on a mortgage.

  • Warranty, special warranty, quit claim, trustee's and life estate deeds are taxable.
  • DOR also lists a deed given instead of foreclosure and an agreement for deed as taxable.
  • A personal representative's deed under a probated will is listed as not taxable.
  • A spousal homestead deed, where the only consideration is a mortgage, and a divorce deed for the marital home are exempt.

sections.h2: What does Florida require for a deed to be recordable?
sections.html:
A deed conveying land must be in writing and signed in front of two witnesses. Section 689.01 requires two subscribing witnesses, no seal, and allows witnessing by audio-video technology.

Before you send a deed to the Clerk, check these points with your title agent:

  • The legal description matches the prior recorded deed.
  • Every owner on record signs, and two witnesses sign for each.
  • The stamp tax is calculated on the right consideration.
  • A lady bird deed has been reviewed by an attorney; a Department of Revenue advisement on one such deed found no present beneficial interest passed and no stamp tax on those facts, but other facts can differ.

sections.h2: How do I protect an Escambia County property from fake deeds?
sections.html:
Sign up for Property Fraud Alert on the Clerk's Landmark Web site. It emails a subscriber each time a land records document is recorded under a name they ask to follow.

The Clerk states that the service is free, does not stop fraud and only reports recorded instruments. Still, an alert on your own name and on the name of a deceased relative on an inherited house gives early warning of a forged deed. The Property Appraiser also notes that if an owner of family property has died and records were never updated, probate or another process may be needed to establish who owns it.

sections.h2: How do I find tax, foreclosure and probate records for a parcel?
sections.html:
Each office has its own record. Tax history sits with the Tax Collector, where taxes become delinquent April 1 and a tax certificate can follow. Foreclosure sales run through the Clerk, and Florida's sale statute directs the clerk to sell between 20 and 35 days after final judgment, with a 5 percent deposit from the high bidder.

For a house with a probate history, ask the Clerk's Public Records Center, which holds probate cases back to 1883 for in-person viewing. A summary administration is available in Florida when the non-exempt estate is $150,000 or less, or the decedent died more than two years earlier.

sections.h2: Does the Escambia Clerk keep marriage records that affect title?
sections.html:
Yes, and they help when a deed signer's name changed or when an heir has to be proved. The Clerk's marriage records from 1996 to the present are held in the Public Records Center, and older books run back to 1822.

  • Marriage books: 1822 to 1999, viewed in person.
  • Microfiche: 1919 through 1995, plus indexes covering 1821 to 1900 and 1901 to 1918.
  • Records from 1996 forward: available through the Clerk's records service.

Pair these with the Landmark Web search, which can return documents by name. A seller whose name differs between the vesting deed and a current ID should gather the marriage or court record that links the names before listing, so a buyer's title company does not stall the closing.

faqs.q: Where are Escambia County deeds recorded?
faqs.a: With the Clerk of the Circuit Court and Comptroller. You can search recorded documents on the Clerk's Landmark Web site by name, book and page, record date and other fields.

faqs.q: What is the stamp tax on a deed in Escambia County?
faqs.a: 70 cents per $100 of consideration, the standard Florida rate. All parties to the deed are liable, and the clerk collects it at recording.

faqs.q: How much is the first page recording fee in Florida?
faqs.a: $5.00 under section 28.24, plus $1.00 to the modernization trust fund and an added $4 per page technology charge. Each added page is $4.00 plus further charges.

faqs.q: Can I view Escambia County probate files from the 1800s online?
faqs.a: No. The Clerk lists old wills, probate cases from 1883 to 1997 and civil files from 1820 to 1985 as viewable only in the Public Records Center.

faqs.q: Does Escambia County offer an alert for fraudulent deeds?
faqs.a: Yes. The Clerk's Property Fraud Alert emails you when a document is recorded under a name you follow. It is free but does not prevent fraud.
